newsitem.title: USA: Ohio's corn nine percent harvested vs 24 average.
newsitem.headline: Ohio's corn nine percent harvested vs 24 average.

text.p: Ohio's corn crop was nine percent harvested as of Sunday, down from 24 percent for the five-year average, the Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop report.
Fifty-six percent of the crop was mature, below the 88 percent average.
Corn was rated five percent very poor, 15 percent poor, 38 percent fair, 36 percent good and six percent excellent.
Soybean harvest was 22 percent complete, down from the 59 percent average, and 90 percent of the plants were dropping leaves, versus the 100 percent average.
Soybeans were rated four percent very poor, 15 percent poor, 37 percent fair, 36 percent good and eight percent excellent.

Winter wheat had emerged on 10 percent of the acreage, slightly behind the 19 percent average. Thirty-five percent of the winter wheat crop was seeded, compared with 74 percent last year and 61 percent on average.

Pasture conditions were four percent very poor, 11 percent poor, 35 percent fair, 45 percent good and five percent excellent. Topsoil was seven percent short, 82 percent adequate and 11 percent surplus.
